claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Biosensors and BioMEMS: A Survey of the Present Field", series "Acquisition Threat Support", published 2010-03-31 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2009-12-01, DIA document number DIA-08-1003-020. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.
Released PDF is 45 pages, marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO caveat partially illegible in the scan).
Entry 6 on the DIA list transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee on 9 January 2018 reads 'Biosensors and BioMEMS, Dr Bruce Towe, Univ of Arizona.'

The released cover page carries the date 31 March 2010, an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 1 December 2009 and document number DIA-08-1003-020; the author field is redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(5) and 'Prepared by' is redacted under 10 U.S.C. 424.

The administrative note states the product 'is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency ... Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program.'

Contents cover brain-implanted BioMEMS micromachine neuroelectrodes, implantable sensors, microelectrode array fabrication, brain-machine interfaces, polymer BioMEMS electrodes, retinal devices and therapeutic neurostimulation - the human-effects and human-interface leg of the AAWSAP survey.

connections.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
connections.note: The document's own administrative note states it 'is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency ... Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program', with comments directed to the AAWSA Program Manager, DIA, Bldg 6000, Washington DC 20340-5100. Hal Puthoff, subcontracting to BAASS through EarthTech International, has stated he let the 38 contracts himself, acting as a surrogate so DIA would not have to expose its interest.
